text:
Maya (Support): FYI priority customer ZetaCorp reporting p99 latency spikes ~4x starting 00:30 UTC after their invoice-cycle window. They're seeing 10-15s p99 on text-generation endpoints. Ticket #CS-4529.
Aria (Customer Success): Customer is in Prod, high traffic after billing window. They called and are very upset. Need triage fast. :grimacing: @Jordan can you take lead?
Jordan (SRE): On it. Can you paste the request IDs / sample logs?
Maya (Support): Pasted a few in the ticket: reqs: req-8a3f, req-8b12, req-8c44. Also attached p95/p99 graphs from console.
Jordan (SRE): Looking at traces: attach latency + scale-up queue time increased at 00:28. Several attach attempts failed with attach_timeout and then retried, causing thundering fanout.
Sam (Oncall): I'm seeing a spike in pool attach throttles on dedicated-pool-us-west-2-dedicated-42. Warm pool min=0 so cold starts are happening. CPU/GPU provisioning looks fine but VM boot + init of kernels (model cache) is ~6-8s per attach. Retries stack up.
Priya (Eng-Platform): Two things to confirm: did Dedicated autoscale policy recently change? I see a config push at 00:10 that set aggressive scale-down to free capacity during low-usage windows.
Nikhil (Runtime): Confirmed: scale-down-policy.yaml was deployed at 00:09 with min_idle=0 for that tier. That explains low warm capacity before the overnight surge.
Jordan (SRE): That matches timeline: scale-down left no warm GPUs, invoice-cycle surge hits, many concurrent attach requests -> cold GPU start + kernel JIT/quant table loads -> p99 blow up.
Aria (Customer Success): Customer wants root cause + ETA for fix. They're sensitive - contract SLAs.
Maya (Support): Customer also reported some 401s around 00:33 but those look unrelated (short token refresh errors). Main complaint is latency.
Jordan (SRE): Immediate mitigations being considered: 1) temporary increase warm pool min for the customer/tier, 2) route ZetaCorp traffic to backup reserved pool with warmer instances, 3) apply short-term attach backoff and prioritize existing sessions. Thoughts?
Priya (Eng-Platform): We can bump min_warm for that dedicated pool to 2-4 immediately. Also we have a prewarm job that can be triggered to populate model cache (kv cache + kernels). I'll run that.
Nikhil (Runtime): Prewarm will cut per-attach model-init time from ~6s to ~0.5s once kernels/caches are hot. But need a couple minutes to warm.
Sam (Oncall): I'll open an emergency runbook action: increase warm pool min to 3 -> trigger prewarm for model redwood-v2-medium on that pool -> temporarily raise attach concurrency limit to reduce retry storms.
deploy-bot: runbook:apply change scale-settings --pool dedicated-42 --min_warm 3 --by sam --start 1799991455
Jordan (SRE): After applying min_warm=3 and firing prewarm, p99 dropped to ~2.1s within 7 minutes. p95 back to baseline. Rechecking customer graphs.
Aria (Customer Success): I told ZetaCorp we have a mitigation and are working on a durable fix. They're OK for now but want permanent prevention.
Priya (Eng-Platform): Permanent fixes: 1) avoid min_warm=0 for tiers with invoice/cron surges, 2) scheduled prewarm hooks tied to customer billing cycles, 3) smarter scale-down hysteresis during known burst windows. I'll open an RFC for the orchestration change.
Nikhil (Runtime): Also propose a fast-path for kernel preloading: if a burst is detected, kick async cache pull to GPU ahead of attach completion. Lower-risk patch we can land quickly.
Jordan (SRE): Short-term config changes: add a policy exception for priority customers so their dedicated pools keep min_warm>=2 by default. Medium term: scheduled prewarm + hysteresis. Long term: improve attach backoff jitter to avoid retry storms.
Maya (Support): Noted. Customer-facing note prepared: "We identified autoscaling and cold-GPU starts as the root cause; we applied a temporary warm-pool bump and prewarm, which reduced p99. Engineering is implementing durable mitigations." Sending now.
Aria (Customer Success): Customer appreciated the quick update. They asked for timeline on RFC and ETA for platform change. Priya, can you give a rough estimate?
Priya (Eng-Platform): RFC by EOD, implementation plan in 1 sprint (2 weeks) for scheduled prewarm + policy exceptions. Kernel async preload maybe 3 sprints.
Jordan (SRE): Postmortem items: - revert overly aggressive scale-down default, - add monitoring alert when warm_pool count==0 and attach rate > X, - add RBAC for rapid warm bump with audit trail.
Sam (Oncall): I'll capture metrics and attach traces for the postmortem. Exporting logs and request IDs to CS ticket.
Maya (Support): Closing loop: customer updated, ticket flagged as escalated -> resolved for now. Will monitor 24h.
Nikhil (Runtime): One extra note: we also saw a small subset of requests with model cache eviction due to memory pressure on nodes that had been rapidly consolidated. We'll add a guard to prefer eviction-tolerant nodes later.
Jordan (SRE): Thanks team. If anyone sees a recurrence, @here escalate immediately. :thumbsup:
Aria (Customer Success): I'll keep the customer posted. Great work.
Maya (Support): Thread summary: root cause autoscale->min_warm=0 + invoice-cycle burst -> cold GPU attach + kernel init -> attach retries -> p95/p99 spike. Mitigations applied: bump warm pool, trigger prewarm, throttle retries, route if needed. Next steps RFC + postmortem.
